title: Add runbook + on-call playbook for provision-to-ready failures (Dedicated/GPU fleet)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
body:
## Context
We are rolling out automated provision-to-ready for Dedicated pools. Early rollout + incident learnings showed that failures are hard to triage without a single canonical runbook: ownership boundaries (Infra vs Platform vs SRE) are fuzzy, and responders aren’t sure when to retry, reimage, quarantine, or escalate.

This ticket produces:
- A runbook for common provision-to-ready failure modes, keyed off readiness state + failure reason.
- A minimal on-call playbook (first 30 minutes) including escalation paths and “safe actions”.
- Links to dashboards, logs, and the incident template.

References / inputs:
- Slack threads: metric cardinality incident + mitigation (sources/slack/incidents/1739883310.json), quarantine policy discussion (sources/slack/eng-infra/1739237721.json), on-call prep thread (sources/slack/eng-oncall/1739799088.json), NCCL flakes (sources/slack/eng-infra/1739399020.json)
- Dashboard work: ENG-4827 (step breakdown dashboard)
- Readiness API/state machine: ENG-4822 + ADR-017
- Retry/backoff + quarantine defaults: ENG-4825

## Deliverables
### 1) Runbook (triage guide)
Confluence draft already exists, but needs tightening and review for safe remediation order.
Target location:
- sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/provision-to-ready-failures-triage-runbook.json

Minimum sections:
1. **Quick glossary**
   - Readiness states: Allocated / Provisioning / Validating / Ready / Quarantined
   - “Failure reason” field and where it’s authored (validation agent vs control plane)
   - Definition of “time-to-ready” timestamps used by SLOs

2. **First checks (always)**
   - Confirm pool + region + GPU type, image channel (candidate/stable)
   - Confirm whether rollout feature flag is enabled for this pool/region
   - Check if we are in an active rollout window (release train notes) before making changes

3. **Decision tree / safe remediation order**
   - If stuck in **Provisioning**: check cloud-init / kubelet join / CNI readiness
   - If stuck in **Validating**: check which validation step is failing (GPU health / driver parity / network / NCCL / perf canary)
   - If repeated failures: **drain -> quarantine** (do not keep retrying indefinitely)
   - Reimage guidance: when it’s safe, when to avoid due to potential image regression

4. **Failure mode playbooks (common)**
   - **Driver parity mismatch**
     - Symptoms: validation reason includes “driver_version_mismatch” or toolkit mismatch
     - Where to look: validation agent logs; image metadata tags; node labels
     - Safe action: quarantine + reimage to current stable; if spike after image promotion, halt rollout + consider rollback
     - Escalate to Release Eng (Sahana Iyer) if candidate/stable promotion suspected

   - **GPU health failures (ECC / Xid codes / NVML)**
     - Symptoms: “gpu_health_failed” w/ Xid/ECC counters
     - Safe action: quarantine node; do not recycle into serving
     - When to open cloud provider ticket vs RMA path (if applicable)
     - Escalation: Infra/Fleet primary (Vanessa Ortiz), SRE secondary for fleet-wide impact

   - **Kubelet join / node never registers**
     - Symptoms: no heartbeat to readiness service; state doesn’t advance from Provisioning
     - Where to look: cloud-init logs, kubelet status, node bootstrap tokens
     - Safe action: terminate + reprovision (if early in bring-up); avoid manual edits on node

   - **NCCL smoke test flakes / fabric issues**
     - Symptoms: intermittent NCCL timeout; higher in one AZ / instance family
     - Where to look: step traces + canary logs; compare other nodes in same rack/AZ
     - Safe action: one retry max; if persistent: quarantine; raise severity if correlated to a single AZ
     - Escalate: Nina Petrova (architecture) if fabric issue suspected; SRE if error budget at risk

   - **Perf canary regression**
     - Symptoms: perf canary fails threshold after provisioning (latency or throughput)
     - Safe action: mark node not-ready; do not add to serving pool; compare image version and runtime build
     - Escalate: Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor) if readiness gating behaves unexpectedly

   - **Metrics/telemetry issues (cardinality / missing spans)**
     - Symptoms: dashboards broken; alerts noisy; suspected per-node tag explosion
     - Safe action: disable alert rules / switch to ticket-only; stop rollout if can’t observe
     - Link: incident notes around tag explosion and follow-up PR

5. **Escalation paths + ownership**
   - Paged incidents impacting pool readiness/SLOs:
     - Primary: SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher org); Secondary: Infra/Fleet on-call
   - Non-urgent validation tuning / flakes:
     - Create Linear issue; assign Aisha Bello (alerts), Sergio Costa (dashboards), or Infra owner depending on root cause
   - Image build/promotion issues:
     - Release Eng (Sahana Iyer / Connor O’Brien)
   - Control-plane readiness service/API issues:
     - Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor)

6. **Stop-the-line criteria (rollout guardrails)**
   - Validation failure rate > threshold for 30m (per SLO doc)
   - Quarantine count rising and causing capacity shortfall
   - Observability degraded (dashboards/SLIs missing) during rollout

### 2) On-call playbook (first 30 minutes)
Short, copy/pastable checklist intended for responders:
- Identify affected pools + current states
- Determine if this is localized (single pool/AZ) vs systemic (fleet-wide)
- Decide on immediate mitigation (pause rollout flag, quarantine offenders, rollback image channel)
- Communicate in #eng-infra and open an incident if customer capacity impacted

### 3) Incident template integration
Ensure responders have an incident template for provisioning failures.
Link:
- sources/github/incident-bot/pr-118-add-template-for-provisioning-failure-incidents.json

## Acceptance criteria
- Runbook reviewed by Infra/Fleet + SRE (at minimum Vanessa Ortiz + Rafael Mendes) and “safe remediation order” approved.
- Playbook includes:
  - dashboards links
  - readiness state + failure reason interpretation
  - explicit escalation contacts + when to page
- References added to internal docs PR:
  - sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-921-internal-docs-provision-to-ready-operations.json
- Includes note on known issues discovered in staged rollout (metric tag explosion + NCCL flake guidance).

## Open questions
- For quarantine: do we auto-open a ticket to cloud provider after N GPU health failures in same AZ? (Proposed: yes, but defer automation; document manual steps.)
- For image rollback: who has final authority during off-hours (SRE vs Release Eng)? (Proposed: SRE can halt rollout + pin stable; Release Eng required for candidate->stable changes.)

## Links
- ADR readiness state machine: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-017-provision-to-ready-readiness-state-machine.json
- SLO policy: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/provision-to-ready-slo-and-error-budget.json
- Dashboards: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/provision-to-ready-dashboards.json
- Game day plan: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/provision-to-ready-gameday-plan.json
- Related PRs:
  - Metrics step breakdown + cardinality fix: sources/github/redwood/pr-18441-emit-provision-to-ready-metrics-step-breakdown.json, sources/github/redwood/pr-18475-fix-metric-cardinality-in-provisioning-step-tags.json
  - Quarantine behavior: sources/github/redwood/pr-18452-quarantine-nodes-on-repeat-validation-failures.json
  - Docs: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-921-internal-docs-provision-to-ready-operations.json

## Implementation plan
1. Incorporate feedback from #eng-oncall thread: add explicit “when to quarantine vs reimage” and warn against repeated manual tinkering on nodes.
2. Tighten failure-mode sections to map directly to readiness failure reason strings (as emitted by validation agent / readiness service).
3. Add top 5 queries/links:
   - readiness service events by pool
   - validation agent logs
   - step breakdown dashboard
   - quarantine counts
   - SLI time-to-ready charts
4. Add a one-page playbook (Confluence snippet) and link it from dashboards and incident template.

## Rollout / comms
- Post final runbook link in #eng-infra, #eng-sre, #eng-oncall.
- During staged rollout week, pin playbook in #eng-oncall and ensure SRE paging runbook references it.
comments: 2025-10-04 (Harish Reddy): Started consolidating failure modes from Slack threads and the early rollout notes. Biggest gap right now is a clear 'safe actions' section (drain/quarantine/reimage ordering) + ownership boundaries.

2025-10-07 (Rafael Mendes): Please add explicit criteria for when to page SRE vs create ticket. Also call out that during rollout we prefer pausing flags over repeated retries if we can’t observe (dashboards down).
2025-10-10 (Vanessa Ortiz): Add GPU health thresholds we agreed on (ECC/Xid quarantine-worthy) and a warning about not reusing quarantined nodes for serving without a clean reimage + revalidation.

2025-10-12 (Aisha Bello): For alert-related failure modes, point to the tuning notes and make it clear which alerts are paging vs ticket-only during first rollout. Also link the cardinality incident as a 'known pitfall'.
2025-10-15 (Connor O’Brien): Add release train note: any candidate->stable promotion needs Release Eng approval; SRE can pin to stable / pause rollout as mitigation. Keep this crisp for on-call.
2025-10-18 (Sahana Iyer): +1 to calling out image channel + version early in the checklist. Also include where to verify image provenance tags and where to find last promotion audit events.

2025-10-21 (Harish Reddy): Updated runbook with explicit escalation matrix and stop-the-line criteria. Added links to incident template + docs PR. Requesting final review from Vanessa + Rafael before marking Done.
